quickStart: For an immediate police emergency, call 999. For an ambulance or fire emergency, call 995.
For urgent but non-emergency medical needs, contact a healthcare provider or use the official MOH and HealthHub service directories.
Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, CPF, SRS, and essential liabilities.
If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and contact CPF Board, banks, insurers, employers, IRAS, and service providers using their official processes.
CPF nominations and wills are not interchangeable. Confirm CPF nomination status with CPF Board and obtain legal advice for estate questions.
Keep the export encrypted. Never store passwords, Singpass credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes: This guide is general information, not legal, tax, insurance, or financial advice.
Singapore public healthcare subsidies and schemes have eligibility and programme conditions; MediSave is a savings scheme for approved healthcare expenses, not a universal insurance policy.
NRIC/FIN is sensitive personal data. Singapore government guidance says an IC is compulsory for citizens and permanent residents from age 15; recording the number in this organizer is optional.
CPF savings and CPF nominations have specific CPF Board rules and are not interchangeable with a will. Verify current nomination status and distribution procedures directly with CPF Board.

Singapore LPAs are registered arrangements for property/affairs and/or personal welfare decisions if mental capacity is lost. An LPA does not replace a will or determine post-death estate distribution.
IRAS states estate duty was removed for deaths on or after 15 February 2008; confirm any historical or current tax/reporting issue with IRAS or a qualified adviser.
Emergency: Singapore Civil Defence Force: https://www.scdf.gov.sg/

fileStructure: The export ZIP may contain a spreadsheet, PDFs, and this access guide.
Treat every file as sensitive; it may include identity, health, financial, and legal references.
dataAccess: Extract to a private, encrypted location and keep an untouched backup.
Share only with trusted authorised people; a family relationship alone does not grant legal access.
Store credentials in a reputable password manager with an emergency-access feature, not in this export.
securityTips: Never put passwords, PINs, Singpass credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in the export.
Use encrypted storage and secure channels for sensitive documents.
Review after major life events and at least annually; remove outdated copies securely.

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Singapore. Confirm representative authority and current CPF, court, tax, and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Singapore
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow official registration guidance, identify the executor or authorised representative, contact each provider, and keep a record of each action.

startHere: Follow the official death registration and funeral guidance.
Locate the will and identify the executor; check whether probate or letters of administration are required.
Contact CPF Board, IRAS, banks, insurers, employers, SRS operators, and service providers using their current procedures.
List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm authority before changing payments or distributing property.
Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use the deceased person's Singpass or online account credentials.
legalFramework: Singapore Courts probate and letters of administration processes.
CPF Board account, nomination, and death-benefit rules.
IRAS income tax and any estate or historical tax matters.
MSF Office of the Public Guardian LPA registration and decision-support requirements.
Insurance, SRS, property, and financial-institution contract rules.

phases.title: Register and establish authority
phases.focus: Follow official death processes, locate the will, and identify who may act.

keyActions.action: Follow current registration, funeral, and death-certificate instructions from the relevant Singapore agencies.
keyActions.why: The documents and process required depend on circumstances and the agencies involved.

keyActions.action: Find the will and confirm the executor; obtain legal advice if there is no will, a dispute, or a complex estate.
keyActions.why: The executor or administrator may need a court grant before dealing with assets.

mustHaveDocuments: Bank, insurance, property, and liability references
criticalMistakes: Assuming next of kin automatically has authority
Assuming CPF savings follow the will
Putting Singpass or bank credentials in an export

phases.title: Notify and identify claims
phases.focus: Notify CPF, IRAS, financial institutions, employers, and insurers; preserve an accurate inventory.

keyActions.action: Contact CPF Board about CPF savings, any nomination, and the deceased member process.
keyActions.why: CPF distribution follows CPF legislation and nomination procedures, which are distinct from will administration.

keyActions.action: Notify banks, insurers, employers, SRS operators, IRAS, and utilities separately.
keyActions.why: No single notification completes all private claims or account administration.

mustHaveDocuments: List of recurring payments and liabilities
criticalMistakes: Assuming CPF nomination and will are the same

phases.title: Administer and finalise
phases.focus: Complete any required court, IRAS, property, and provider steps before final distribution.

keyActions.action: Confirm whether probate or letters of administration are required under the current Singapore Courts process.
keyActions.why: Requirements depend on the estate, the will, and the organisations holding assets.

keyActions.action: Check outstanding income-tax or historical estate-duty questions with IRAS before distributing assets.
keyActions.why: Tax status depends on dates, income, assets, and current or historical rules.

mustHaveDocuments: CPF, SRS, property, and insurance records
criticalMistakes: Distributing estate assets before confirming authority
Assuming there are no tax or reporting steps

phases.title: Review family arrangements
phases.focus: Review the surviving household's will, LPA, ACP, CPF nominations, and secure recordkeeping.

keyActions.action: Review wills, LPA donees, Advance Care Plans, CPF nominations, insurance, and emergency contacts with appropriate professionals.
keyActions.why: Appointments and nominations may need updating after a major family change.

keyActions.action: Keep an asset and digital-account index; store credentials only in a suitable password manager.
keyActions.why: A secure index helps authorised people find records without exposing secrets.

criticalMistakes: Storing credentials in spreadsheets or PDFs

emergency.crisisSupport: SOS 1767; confirm current service information at sos.org.sg

cpf.note: Check current CPF nomination and member death-process requirements directly with CPF Board.

estate.note: Confirm whether probate or letters of administration are required with Singapore Courts.

glossary.definition: A CPF Board nomination specifying who is to receive CPF savings under CPF rules; it is not the same as a will.
A registered legal document appointing donees to make specified personal-welfare and/or property-and-affairs decisions if the donor loses mental capacity.
A court grant that authorises the executor named in a will to administer the estate when a grant is required.
